subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs InferX vs OpenServe - Acme
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@acmecorp.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs InferX vs OpenServe - Acme

Hi Daniel / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our end and proposed next steps so we stay aligned heading into the bake-off.

Pain points you confirmed:
- High per-call latency on your current vendor during peak traffic (95th percentile spikes > 900ms for 2k context).
- Token costs are ~2.8x higher than internal target for summarization workloads.
- Need strong controls around data residency, audit logs, and SSO for any production path.

Goal / decision criteria (what Acme told us matters most):
1) 95th percentile latency under 400ms for standard 1k-context queries.
2) Total cost-per-1M tokens (in production profile) with batching/caching enabled.
3) Reproducible quality on your summarization prompt set (F1 / ROUGE targets TBD).
4) Security/compliance: SOC 2, SSO, and audit log retention.

Competitive notes from the call:
- InferX: good latency but higher cost at scale and limited KV-cache support for long sessions.
- OpenServe: easy integration, weaker throughput under batching.
- Redwood: our focus will be on predictable latency + cost controls (batching, prefix cache) and an evaluation harness you can run locally or in your VPC.

Open questions / actions for Acme:
- Please share the canonical prompt set and a representative sample of 10k queries (anonymized) for the bake-off.
- Confirm whether the test should run in your AWS account (preferred) or in our sandbox.
- Success metric weighting: what % of the decision is latency vs cost vs quality?

Proposed bake-off plan (timeline):
- This week (by Fri, Apr 9): Acme shares prompt set + success weights.
- Week of Apr 12: Redwood / InferX / OpenServe run parallel tests on the same dataset.
- Apr 20: Joint review + side-by-side results (latency, cost, quality).

Next steps from Redwood:
- Aditya (cc'd) will put together a technical test plan (benchmarks, how we measure token cost, and the scoring script).
- I will share a short summary PDF with test assumptions and the evaluation sheet.

Attachments: redwood_bakeoff_eval_20270405.pdf (overview + scoring rubric), acme_sample_prompts.txt (placeholder)

If that plan looks good, we can lock in the test window and I can schedule a 30-min sync to iron out the dataset transfer and access model.

Thanks — speak soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0124

--
Redwood Inference
Making inference predictable and economical for production apps
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@acmecorp.com>

Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs InferX vs OpenServe - Acme

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. That matches our notes. A few quick clarifications: 

- We'll provide the 10k anonymized queries by end of day Thu (want to run a quick scrub first).
- Procurement requires SOC 2 evidence and our IdP/SSO SAML flow to be validated before any production pilots. Can you include a SOC 2 cert copy and an SSO integration checklist?
- For decision weighting, our committee is thinking ~40% latency, 30% cost, 30% quality — but we can finalize after we see the first results.

We prefer the tests run in our AWS account (gives us confidence on network/egress cost). Priya will share an IAM role for the infra team to use.

Also can you include a simple latency/cost worksheet so the procurement team can model annual spend? That'll help speed the committee review.

Looking forward to the plan from Aditya.

Best,
Daniel
Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Corp

Target: have both deliverables ready by Fri Apr 9 so we can start the run week of Apr 12.
